title: The Day the Overdue Clock Runs From on a Retrofit Project
content:
# The Day the Overdue Clock Runs From on a Retrofit Project

A payment on account restarts the overdue clock on a project under Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects, and where nothing has yet fallen due no clock runs at all.

**Where a payment has been received on the project after the day the most recent progress billing fell due**, the overdue clock runs from the day of that payment.

**Where no payment has been received after that day and a progress billing has fallen due**, the overdue clock runs from the day the most recent progress billing fell due.

**Where no progress billing has fallen due on the project**, no overdue clock runs and no late fee is raised.

## What is read

The day the most recent progress billing fell due is the latest due day among the progress billings on the project's record. The payment read is the most recent payment received on the project. A payment dated on the due day itself is not after it, so the clock still runs from the due day.

| Most recent progress billing due day | Most recent payment received | The clock runs from |
|---|---|---|
| the 10th | the 14th | the 14th |
| the 10th | the 10th | the 10th |
| the 10th | the 2nd | the 10th |
| the 10th | none | the 10th |
| none on the record | any or none | no clock runs, and no late fee is raised |

## Cases (hypothetical, fee raised on the 30th)

A progress billing fell due on the 10th and a payment came in on the 14th: the clock runs from the 14th and the days overdue are 16. The same project with no payment after the 10th: the clock runs from the 10th and the days overdue are 20. A project whose only billings are the deposit and the mobilisation fee, with no progress billing yet due: no clock runs and no late fee is raised.
